name: sys_netcontrol netevent double fdrop - double put of a struct file

root_cause.summary: kern_netevent_clear_queue() finds the netevent entry by the socket fd supplied by the caller, clears the entry, and then calls fdrop() twice: once for the reference the netevent took when the socket was added and once for getsock_cap()'s own reference. The entry stores only the fd number, not the file pointer, so the lookup can be made to match the wrong socket: add s1 (refcount 2), close s1 (1), create s2 which reuses s1's fd (1), then clear with s2's fd. bnet_netevent_clear_queue() does not match, so the 'netevent' fdrop lands on s2, which drops to refcount 0 while the fd table still references it, and s1's reference is leaked. The freed file stays reachable through the descriptor; on PS4 fcntl(F_SETFL) calls fhold()/fdrop() directly and frees it again, while on PS5 fcntl goes through fget() and hangs on the zero refcount, so the public PS5 trigger is dup().
root_cause.primitive: double fput of struct file, leaving a freed file reachable from the descriptor table
root_cause.trigger: netcontrol(if_index 0, cmd 0x20000003) with s1's fd, close(s1), socket() to reuse the fd, netcontrol(cmd 0x20000007) with the new fd, then dup() (PS5) or fcntl(F_SETFL) (PS4) to use the stale file
root_cause.consequence: use-after-free of a file/socket object; the public implementation converts it into arbitrary kernel read/write by corrupting a pipebuf buffer pointer, then jailbreaks

discovery_approach.summary: slidybat reported the fd-reuse mismatch to PlayStation's HackerOne programme on 2025-08-30 (report 3320669, severity high, $10,000, disclosed 2026-05-01). The report quotes the pre-fix set/clear handlers, gives the five-step reproduction and notes the platform difference in fcntl. TheFloW published a BD-J implementation chained with BD-JB3 (PS4) and BD-JB2 (PS5) on 2025-11-02, and Gezine chained it with PS5 BD-JB-EX in 2026.
signals: a clear/remove handler that compares a stored fd number with a caller-supplied fd instead of comparing struct file pointers
two consecutive fdrop() calls on the same struct file in one success path
a reference taken by getsock_cap() that is not distinguished from the reference owned by the netevent entry
an fd table entry that still points at a file whose refcount already reached zero

differences: the defect itself is the fd-value comparison in the netevent lookup: an fd recycled by close() + socket() defeats the match and the second fdrop lands on a file that never held the reference

PS4 and PS5 differ only in the use primitive: PS4's fcntl(F_SETFL) calls fhold()/fdrop() without fget(), so it frees the stale file again, while PS5's fcntl goes through fget() and the zero refcount makes it hang - which is why the public PS5 trigger is dup()
the fix landed in PS5 12.02 and PS4 13.02 per the dev wiki; no post-fix code or diff is public

patch_evidence.what: the disclosed HackerOne report supplies the pre-fix kern_netevent_set_queue/clear_queue code and the exact reproduction; the dev wiki supplies the first fixed versions (PS5 12.02, PS4 13.02)
patch_evidence.limits: the post-fix handler is not shown and no vendor diff was published; the fix mechanism can only be inferred from the defect

sources.supports: the whole mechanism: getsock_cap() reference owned by the netevent, two fdrop() calls in the clear path, fd-number comparison instead of file-pointer comparison, the five-step reproduction, PS4 fcntl(F_SETFL) re-freeing the file vs PS5 fget() hanging, weakness 'Double Free', disclosed 2026-05-01

PS4 affected through 13.00 and fixed in 13.02; credits slidybat (discovery 2025-08-30) and TheFloW (public implementation 2025-11-02); the note that PS5 needs dup() because unprivileged libkernel lacks a dup wrapper
PS5 affected through 12.00 and fixed in 12.02, plus the implementation list (TheFloW 2025-11-02, Gezine 2026-05-03)

the public implementation's use of __sys_netcontrol cmd 0x20000003/0x20000007, dup(), kqueue/pipe primitives, and its conversion of the file UAF into arbitrary R/W by overwriting a pipebuf's buffer pointer

gaps: the report does not name the fixed code or the check that was added; only the first fixed versions are public
the PS5 range lower bound is not stated (the wiki section title only gives '<= 12.00')
the exploit's later stages (pipebuf corruption, allproc walk, ucred patch) are specific to the quoted implementation and are not part of the bug description
no source states whether the double fdrop is also reachable from other netcontrol commands or other netevent users
